newsitem.title: USA: Three Georgia school districts ok tax referendums.
newsitem.headline: Three Georgia school districts ok tax referendums.

text.p: Three more Georgia school boards have approved March referendums on a proposed one-cent sales tax increase to fund school construction.
School boards in City of Atlanta and DeKalb and Clayton counties approved the March 18 referendums in meetings Monday night.
The five-year tax would raise $450 million in Atlanta, which would use the money to repair and renovate a dozen schools and retire $141 million of debt.
The tax would raise $381 million in DeKalb County, which would use its revenues to build 11 new schools and pay off $91.2 million in outstanding construction debt.
City of Decatur, a Dekalb County community that operates a separate school system, would receive $15.4 million, or three percent of the couty's tax.
Clayton County's tax would raise $112.6 million, with more than $22 million earmarked for new school contruction.

In November, Georgia voters approved a constitutional amendment allowing school districts to seek one-cent sales tax hikes for five years to build new schools or retire construction debt. Previously, only property taxes could be used or school contruction.
The increase still must be approved in local district referendums before the tax can be levied.
Clarke, Douglas, Fulton, Gwinnett, Meriwether and Paulding counties previously approved March 18 referendums on the tax hike.
